name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICALBONDING_MCQ_Q01 - Energetics of ionic bond formation and lattice stabilization

questiontext.text:
Statement I: In the formation of an ionic compound, the ionization of a gaseous metal atom is always endothermic, whereas electron gain by a gaseous non-metal atom may be exothermic or endothermic.

Statement II: An ionic solid such as \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) is stabilized primarily by its enthalpy of lattice formation rather than simply by achieving an octet of electrons around the gaseous ions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ionic compound formation involves ionization of the metal atom, electron gain by the non-metal atom, and electrostatic assembly of the resulting ions into a three-dimensional crystal lattice.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Removing an electron from a neutral gaseous atom always requires energy, so ionization is always endothermic. By contrast, adding an electron to a neutral gaseous atom (electron gain enthalpy) may release energy (exothermic) or absorb energy (endothermic). Thus, the first claim is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
For \(\mathrm{NaCl}\), the sum of the ionization enthalpy of \(\mathrm{Na}(\mathrm{g})\) (\(+495.8\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)) and electron gain enthalpy of \(\mathrm{Cl}(\mathrm{g})\) (\(-348.7\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)) is positive (\(+147.1\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)), which is more than compensated for by the lattice formation enthalpy (\(-788\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)). Therefore, stability is governed primarily by lattice enthalpy rather than simply achieving an octet in the gas phase. Thus, the second claim is also correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both claims are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICALBONDING_MCQ_Q02 - VSEPR electron-pair repulsion order and multiple bonds

questiontext.text:
Statement I: According to VSEPR theory, the repulsive interaction between two lone pairs is greater than the repulsive interaction between a lone pair and a bond pair.

Statement II: In VSEPR theory, a double bond is treated as two separate electron pairs that exert independent repulsions in different directions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
VSEPR theory predicts molecular shapes by considering the spatial repulsion among electron-density regions around a central atom.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Lone pairs are localised on the central atom and occupy more space than shared bond pairs, so the repulsive interaction decreases in the order \(\mathrm{lp-lp} > \mathrm{lp-bp} > \mathrm{bp-bp}\). Hence, the first claim is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
In VSEPR theory, a multiple bond (double or triple) is treated as if it were a single electron pair (a single super pair), not as separate independent electron pairs. Hence, the second claim is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first claim is correct, whereas the second claim is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICALBONDING_MCQ_Q03 - Resonance canonical forms and hybrid energy

questiontext.text:
Statement I: In the carbonate ion (\(\mathrm{CO}_{3}^{2-}\)), the three canonical forms exist in a rapid dynamic equilibrium with one another, similar to keto–enol tautomerism.

Statement II: The energy of a resonance hybrid is higher than the energy of any single canonical structure.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Resonance describes a single real electronic structure (the resonance hybrid) using multiple hypothetical Lewis structures (canonical forms).

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Canonical forms have no real existence, and there is no dynamic equilibrium between them as exists between tautomeric forms. Thus, the first claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
Resonance stabilizes a molecule or ion because the energy of the resonance hybrid is always less than the energy of any single canonical structure. Thus, the second claim is also incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both claims are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICALBONDING_MCQ_Q04 - Dipole moments of NH3 and NF3

questiontext.text:
Statement I: The net dipole moment of \(\mathrm{NF}_{3}\) is greater than that of \(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\) because fluorine is more electronegative than hydrogen.

Statement II: In \(\mathrm{NF}_{3}\), the orbital dipole due to the lone pair on nitrogen acts in the direction opposite to the resultant dipole moment of the three \(\mathrm{N-F}\) bonds.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Both \(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\) and \(\mathrm{NF}_{3}\) are trigonal pyramidal with one lone pair on nitrogen; the net dipole moment is the vector sum of the lone-pair orbital dipole and the three bond dipoles.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Experimentally, the dipole moment of \(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\) (\(1.47\ \mathrm{D}\) or \(4.90 \times 10^{-30}\ \mathrm{C\ m}\)) is much greater than that of \(\mathrm{NF}_{3}\) (\(0.23\ \mathrm{D}\) or \(0.80 \times 10^{-30}\ \mathrm{C\ m}\)). Hence, the first claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
In \(\mathrm{NF}_{3}\), the \(\mathrm{N-F}\) bond dipoles point toward the more electronegative fluorine atoms, whereas the orbital dipole of the lone pair points away from the fluorine atoms, opposing the resultant of the three \(\mathrm{N-F}\) bond dipoles and reducing the net dipole moment. Hence, the second claim is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first claim is incorrect, while the second claim is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICALBONDING_MCQ_Q05 - Axial and equatorial bonds in PCl5

questiontext.text:
Statement I: In \(\mathrm{PCl}_{5}\), the two axial \(\mathrm{P-Cl}\) bonds are slightly longer and weaker than the three equatorial \(\mathrm{P-Cl}\) bonds.

Statement II: In trigonal bipyramidal \(\mathrm{PCl}_{5}\), the axial bond pairs suffer greater repulsive interaction from the equatorial bond pairs.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In a trigonal bipyramidal geometry (\(sp^{3}d\) hybridisation), three equatorial bonds lie in one plane at \(120^{\circ}\) to each other, while two axial bonds lie at \(90^{\circ}\) to the equatorial plane.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Experimental measurements confirm that the two axial \(\mathrm{P-Cl}\) bonds are slightly longer and weaker than the three equatorial \(\mathrm{P-Cl}\) bonds, making \(\mathrm{PCl}_{5}\) reactive. Hence, the first claim is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
Each axial bond pair experiences three \(90^{\circ}\) repulsions from the equatorial bond pairs, whereas each equatorial bond pair experiences only two \(90^{\circ}\) repulsions from the axial bond pairs. Thus, axial bond pairs suffer greater repulsion, and the second claim is also correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both claims are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICALBONDING_MCQ_Q06 - Sigma versus pi bond strength and C2 double bond

questiontext.text:
Statement I: A sigma (\(\sigma\)) bond is stronger than a pi (\(\pi\)) bond because axial orbital overlapping occurs to a larger extent than sidewise overlapping.

Statement II: According to molecular orbital theory, the double bond in the \(\mathrm{C}_{2}\) molecule consists of one \(\sigma\) bond and one \(\pi\) bond.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Bond strength in valence bond theory depends on the extent of orbital overlap, while molecular orbital theory determines the \(\sigma\) and \(\pi\) character of bonds from occupied MOs.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Axial (head-on) overlapping in a \(\sigma\) bond occurs to a greater extent than sidewise overlapping in a \(\pi\) bond, making the \(\sigma\) bond stronger. Thus, the first claim is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
For \(\mathrm{C}_{2}\), the MO configuration is \(\mathrm{KK}(\sigma 2s)^{2}(\sigma^{*} 2s)^{2}(\pi 2p_{x}^{2} = \pi 2p_{y}^{2})\). Since the four net bonding electrons occupy two \(\pi\) molecular orbitals, the double bond in \(\mathrm{C}_{2}\) consists of both \(\pi\) bonds, not one \(\sigma\) and one \(\pi\) bond. Thus, the second claim is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first claim is correct, whereas the second claim is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICALBONDING_MCQ_Q07 - MO energy ordering and bond order of N2 and N2+

questiontext.text:
Statement I: For the \(\mathrm{N}_{2}\) molecule, the \(\sigma 2p_{z}\) molecular orbital has lower energy than the degenerate \(\pi 2p_{x}\) and \(\pi 2p_{y}\) molecular orbitals.

Statement II: When \(\mathrm{N}_{2}\) loses one electron to form \(\mathrm{N}_{2}^{+}\), its bond order increases from \(3.0\) to \(3.5\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In homonuclear diatomic molecules up to \(\mathrm{N}_{2}\), \(2s\text{-}2p\) mixing alters the relative energies of the \(\sigma 2p_{z}\) and \(\pi 2p\) molecular orbitals, and bond order is given by \(\frac{1}{2}(N_{b} - N_{a})\).

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
For \(\mathrm{B}_{2}\), \(\mathrm{C}_{2}\), and \(\mathrm{N}_{2}\), the energy of \(\sigma 2p_{z}\) is higher than that of \(\pi 2p_{x}\) and \(\pi 2p_{y}\) (\(\pi 2p_{x} = \pi 2p_{y} < \sigma 2p_{z}\)). Thus, the first claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
In \(\mathrm{N}_{2}\), \(N_{b} = 10\) and \(N_{a} = 4\), giving \(\mathrm{BO} = \frac{1}{2}(10 - 4) = 3.0\). Removing one electron from the highest occupied bonding orbital (\(\sigma 2p_{z}\)) gives \(\mathrm{N}_{2}^{+}\) with \(N_{b} = 9\) and \(N_{a} = 4\), so \(\mathrm{BO} = \frac{1}{2}(9 - 4) = 2.5\) (a decrease, not an increase). Thus, the second claim is also incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both claims are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICALBONDING_MCQ_Q08 - Hybridisation changes in BF3.NH3 and AlCl4- formation

questiontext.text:
Statement I: In the reaction \(\mathrm{BF}_{3} + \mathrm{NH}_{3} \rightarrow \mathrm{F}_{3}\mathrm{B}\cdot\mathrm{NH}_{3}\), both boron and nitrogen atoms change their hybridisation from \(sp^{2}\) to \(sp^{3}\).

Statement II: In the reaction \(\mathrm{AlCl}_{3} + \mathrm{Cl}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{AlCl}_{4}^{-}\), the hybridisation of the aluminium atom changes from \(sp^{2}\) to \(sp^{3}\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The hybridisation of a central atom is determined by the total number of \(\sigma\) bonds and lone pairs around it.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
In \(\mathrm{BF}_{3} + \mathrm{NH}_{3} \rightarrow \mathrm{F}_{3}\mathrm{B}\cdot\mathrm{NH}_{3}\), boron goes from \(3\sigma\) bonds (\(sp^{2}\)) to \(4\sigma\) bonds (\(sp^{3}\)). However, nitrogen in \(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\) has \(3\sigma\) bonds and \(1\) lone pair (\(sp^{3}\)), and in the adduct it has \(4\sigma\) bonds (\(sp^{3}\)); thus nitrogen does not change its hybridisation. Therefore, the first claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
In \(\mathrm{AlCl}_{3}\), aluminium has \(3\sigma\) bonds and no lone pairs (\(sp^{2}\) hybridised). Upon forming \(\mathrm{AlCl}_{4}^{-}\), aluminium forms \(4\sigma\) bonds with no lone pairs, changing its hybridisation to \(sp^{3}\). Therefore, the second claim is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first claim is incorrect, while the second claim is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
